title: Highly robust molecular information carriers for traceability of plastic materials
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73889-1

Sequence-defined oligomers offer programmable molecular architectures but their deployment in real-world materials has been constrained by their low scale, limited thermal resilience and the need for specialized analytical methods. Here the authors introduce a molecular tagging strategy based on abiotic sequence-defined oligoamides incorporated at ultralow concentrations that endure the thermal and chemical conditions of industrial polymer processing

title: NAD+ modulates mitochondrial vulnerability in MERTK-associated models of retinitis pigmentosa
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74400-6

Retinitis pigmentosa leads to blindness due to photoreceptor loss. Here, the authors show that the NAD+ precursor NMN protects against retinal degeneration by improving mitochondrial function in MERTK-associated models, offering potential therapeutic insights.

title: Ecological multifunctionality of watersheds increases with tree species richness
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74914-z

Watersheds support ecological functions, yet how biodiversity shapes their performance across large landscapes remains unclear. This study finds that higher forest tree diversity increases with watershed multifunctionality, but the effect weakens in arid climates.

title: Multiple human transgenes prolong survival of triple-carbohydrate knockout porcine kidney xenografts in nonhuman primates
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74933-w

Genetically modified pigs lacking the three major carbohydrate xenoantigens (3KO) are being developed to reduce immune rejection in xenotransplantation. Here, the authors evaluate 3KO kidney grafts and show that adding human transgenes, notably TNFAIP3 and HMOX1, dampens immune responses and improves graft survival in non-human primate models

title: Structural basis for multivitamin recognition and transport by human SMVT
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74948-3

Here, Cryo-EM structures of the human SMVT transporter in three distinct conformational states unveil the complete transport cycle and a conserved substrate-binding pocket, elucidating how it recognises and transports multiple essential vitamins.

title: Production of aromatics from high density polyethylene over a hierarchical zeolite synthesised from steam-assisted crystallisation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74562-3

The conversion of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) waste into aromatic feedstocks without using noble-metal catalysts remains a significant challenge. Here, the authors report a steam-assisted synthesized zeolite that enables highly efficient HDPE conversion to aromatics, achieving both high conversion and selectivity at 260 °C and outperforming noble metal-based catalysts under the same conditions.

title: Confined ionic order in atomic nanowires of rare-earth chlorides unveiled via symmetry-guided structural screening
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74793-4

Confined low-dimensional materials offer attractive properties, but their atomic structures are hard to resolve. Here, the authors develop a symmetry-guided imaging and modelling approach to identify rare-earth chloride nanowires confined in carbon nanotubes.

title: Broadband Radiative Heat Transfer Suppression via Dispersion-Engineered Metasurfaces
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74805-3

Radiative heat transfer control is crucial for energy efficiency but limited by bandwidth trade-offs. Here, the authors demonstrate dielectric metasurface pairs with misaligned resonances optimized to suppress heat exchange, achieving up to 82% reduction with a compact, robust, metal-free platform.
